document.title: System
document.subtitle:
Lets organizations manage members, roles, tasks, files and notifications in a CRM, and lets shop customers view products, place and pay for orders.

- auth-service: runs [auth-service](#/containers-service-com-crm-auth-auth-service/el-service-com-crm-auth-auth-service)
- catalog: runs [catalog-service](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service/el-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service)
- catalog-lib: no deployable unit
- crm-shared-lib: no deployable unit
- discovery-and-gateway: runs [api-gateway](#/containers-service-com-crm-auth-auth-service/el-service-com-crm-api-gateway) and [eureka-service](#/containers-service-com-crm-eureka-service/el-service-com-crm-eureka-service)

**Claim the code contradicts**
`README.md`, line 31, in main-service says: “Spring Boot 3.x (parent POM)”. It states Spring Boot 3; the code shows Spring Boot 4.1.1. The code shows otherwise: [main-service](#/containers-service-com-crm-auth-auth-service/el-service-org-springframework-boot-main-service)'s technology is Spring Boot 4.1.1 / Java 25 (`pom.xml`, line 36, in main-service).

**Claim the code contradicts**
`README.md`, line 5, in payments says: “Payments has a database of its own and never reads another service's tables.”. The code shows otherwise: [payments](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-fulfilment/el-service-com-acme-shop-payments) accesses the data of [storefront](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service/el-service-com-acme-shop-storefront-app) (`src/main/java/com/acme/shop/payments/SettlementJob.java`, line 21, in payments).

**Claim the code contradicts**
`README.md`, line 5, in payments says: “Payments has a database of its own and never reads another service's tables.”. The code shows otherwise: [payments](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-fulfilment/el-service-com-acme-shop-payments) uses [shop on shop-db](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-payments/el-database-shop-db-5432-shop) (`src/main/resources/application.properties`, line 5, in payments); [storefront](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service/el-service-com-acme-shop-storefront-app) uses [shop on shop-db](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-payments/el-database-shop-db-5432-shop) (`storefront-app/src/main/resources/application.yml`, line 5, in storefront).

**Claim the code contradicts**
`README.md`, line 5, in storefront says: “Storefront never calls another service synchronously when an order is placed. It publishes an `order.created` event to RabbitMQ and the payments service charges the order from that event.”. The code shows otherwise: [storefront](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service/el-service-com-acme-shop-storefront-app) makes a call Lantern could not link: GET ${TAX_SERVICE_URL}/v2/quotes (`storefront-integration/src/main/java/com/acme/shop/storefront/integration/TaxClient.java`, line 18, in storefront); [storefront](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service/el-service-com-acme-shop-storefront-app) calls [catalog-service](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service/el-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service) (`storefront-integration/src/main/java/com/acme/shop/storefront/integration/CatalogClient.java`, line 11, in storefront); [storefront](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-catalog-service/el-service-com-acme-shop-storefront-app) calls [payments](#/containers-service-com-acme-shop-fulfilment/el-service-com-acme-shop-payments) (`storefront-integration/src/main/java/com/acme/shop/storefront/integration/PaymentsClient.java`, line 21, in storefront).

type-com-crm-auth-cache-userpermissionre.name: UserPermissionRepository
type-com-crm-auth-cache-userpermissionre.description: Purpose inferred from the code: UserPermissionRepository is a Spring repository class in the package com.crm.auth.cache that stores each user's permissions in Redis, keyed by organization and user, with a time limit on how long they remain. It saves and looks up a UserPermission, records a short-lived failure marker when a permission load fails, and hands out a distributed lock per user so that loading happens once at a time. It works mainly with RedisTemplate instances and the RedisLockRegistry, and its key format comes from the shared library's CacheConstants.

type-com-crm-auth-mapper-accesscontrolma.name: AccessControlMapper
type-com-crm-auth-mapper-accesscontrolma.description: Purpose inferred from the code: AccessControlMapper is a Spring component in the package com.crm.auth.mapper that converts a user's roles into the resource permissions the system works with. For each role it reads the stored access control entries and groups their actions by resource, then collapses a resource that has all four basic actions into a single ALL action. It works mainly with Role and AccessControl entities from the auth persistence layer and produces ResourcePermission objects from the shared library.

type-com-crm-auth-service-authentication.name: AuthenticationService
type-com-crm-auth-service-authentication.description: Purpose inferred from the code: AuthenticationService is the Spring service in the com.crm.auth.service package that handles user sign-up, sign-in and logout for the CRM system. It issues a JWT access token and a refresh token for a user, delegating user lookup and creation to UserService and UserCreatorService, token work to JwtService and RefreshTokenService, and device identification to DeviceInfoService. The types it works with most are User, RefreshToken and JwtAuthenticationResponse.

type-com-crm-auth-service-jwtservice.name: JwtService
type-com-crm-auth-service-jwtservice.description: Purpose inferred from the code: JwtService is a Spring service in the package com.crm.auth.service that issues and checks the signed tokens used to identify users of the CRM. It creates a token carrying a user's ID and login, and reads such a token back into a JwtPayload, rejecting it as unauthorized when it is malformed, has a bad signature or has expired. It works with the Claims and SecretKey types of the JJWT library and with the shared JwtPayload and UnauthorizedException classes.

type-com-crm-auth-service-operation-user.name: UserCreatorService
type-com-crm-auth-service-operation-user.description: Purpose inferred from the code: It works mainly with SignUpRequest, User, and PasswordGenerator.

type-com-crm-auth-service-operation-user.name: UserPermissionSaver

It works mainly with the RefreshToken and User entities and the RefreshTokenRepository.

type-com-crm-auth-service-roleservice.name: RoleService

It creates, updates, looks up and deletes roles. It refuses to delete roles marked as non-deletable. It works mainly with the Role entity, the RoleRepository that stores it, the AccessControl entries attached to roles, and the RoleRequest that carries changes.

type-com-crm-auth-service-userpermission.name: UserPermissionService
type-com-crm-auth-service-userpermission.description: Purpose inferred from the code: UserPermissionService is a Spring service class that manages cached permissions for a user within an organization. It saves a user's list of resource permissions as a UserPermission and reads it back. It also handles locking around that data, including setting and checking a failure lock. Its main collaborator is the UserPermissionRepository in com.crm.auth.cache, which holds the stored permissions and locks. It builds UserPermission objects from the shared-library RBAC package.

It enforces that a user may change only their own profile and hashes passwords before saving them. It works mainly with the User entity, its UserRepository, the UserMapper and the sign-up, sign-in and update request objects.

pages.title: POST /api/orders on storefront
pages.summary: A customer's POST to /api/orders on storefront starts the flow. Storefront calls catalog-service over HTTP to fetch the product, saves the order to shop-db, and charges the customer by calling payments over HTTP; payments in turn calls an external payment gateway. Storefront then hands work on asynchronously: it publishes order.created to the shop.orders exchange, which payments consumes, and under the audit profile it also sends a message to audit.orders for fulfilment. Payments publishes payments.completed on Kafka, which fulfilment consumes; fulfilment checks stock with catalog-service, and it dispatches a shipment message that storefront consumes to update the order in shop-db.

sections.title: Overview
rows: POST /api/orders (OrderController.place)
The request must be a POST to /api/orders on storefront. Storefront's configured payments URL resolves to the payments service, and the outbound tax call is not traced.

pages.title: POST /api/auth/sign-up on auth-service
pages.summary: When a client posts to /api/auth/sign-up, auth-service's AuthController hands the request to UserService.createUser, which looks up the login in its UserRepository and raises a conflict error if it already exists.
